description: §66.12.6 rule 1 (a return value carries its return type's grants) + rule 3 (tape methods are named after their grants): `seed() -> int[append]` returns a tape granting `append`, so `const ys = seed(); ys.append(3)` grows it to 3 and one #go click sets @n to 3. XFAIL on impl#1: it cannot prove `ys` is a tape (it types no call result), so it neither implements nor refuses `.append` there; the call reaches the emitted JavaScript and throws `ys.append is not a function` (@n stays 0). The residual of the impl#1 refusal E-IMPL1-RULED-FORM-UNSUPPORTED, carried.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S469 "⭐ RULED — tape methods are named after their grants; JS array method names are refused" ("Names match the grants (Recommended)"); ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S469 "⭐ RULED — impl#1 refuses ruled forms it doesn't implement" ("Refuse them in impl#1 (Recommended)")
rationale: §66.12.6 rule 1: "a return value: what the caller holds carries the return type's grants"; rule 3: `xs.append(x)` is a grow at the end, "Granted by `append`". The tape returned by `seed()` grants `append`, so the call is legal and adds one value.
